extracted.intended_audience: novelists, literary critics, and serious readers of fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and critically reading the modern novel, focused on how novels are made (form, point of view, scene vs. picture, selection and arrangement) and how critics/readers should reconstruct a book to judge it. Emphasizes technical narrative modes and disciplined method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of a book (shape)
rubrics_metrics.description: A book has a form — a shape or design that can be judged as good or bad; it is the object the novelist makes and the critic should try to perceive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the form is hard to grasp because the reader experiences the book as a flowing procession, criticism should aim at the book-as-object: reconstruct the whole, look for a single, coherent outline, and judge whether the form properly expresses the subject. The form is not merely one attribute among many but can be the book itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read aright / constructive critical reading
rubrics_metrics.description: The beginning of criticism is to read aright — to recreate deliberately the book in the reader's mind rather than passively absorb episodes and characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic must stand above the material, keep the novel at a distance so its form can be fashioned, and practice 'creative reading' (Emerson): gather impressions systematically, rebuild the novel as a single object, and thus enable precise discussion of how it was made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist's selection of episodes and arrangement of material is fundamental to making the book an artistic whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the author's choices (what is included, excluded, and how things are ordered) express the subject faithfully and economically. Failures of selection or arrangement produce breaks, divergences, or shapelessness; good selection economizes the novel's effects and yields unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view (choice of stance/center)
rubrics_metrics.description: The point of view determines the book's overall look and is the essential decision after the subject is found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine from which consciousness or stance the story is best told (authorial narrator, dramatized mind, restricted viewpoint, etc.). The point of view controls tone, distance, and methods of presentation and guides which narrative instruments are appropriate at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic incident / the scene
rubrics_metrics.description: The dramatic scene (a direct, acted moment) is the chief and most powerful instrument — the 'final stroke' — but it is costly in time and space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scenes to clinch matters, demonstrate results, or crown effects half-made by other means. Avoid overusing or wasting them: a scene without preparation is inefficient and weakens its climax. Scenes should be placed where their sharpness will have maximal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial narrative / picture (general survey)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictorial or panoramic narrative surveys long reaches of time and space; it accumulates impression rather than dramatizes single moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ picture when breadth and accumulated impression are required; be aware of its inherent thinness as a direct report. Convert that weakness into strength by dramatizing the mind or 'mirror' that reports it (interpose consciousness) so the pictorial mode yields a distinctive effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of narrative (use of oblique or summary methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different narrative modes have different costs: dramatized scenes are time/space-expensive while oblique/narrative summary covers more ground economically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose oblique narrative or summary to convey long periods or distant events with economy, reserving scenes for decisive moments that merit the cost. Failure to economize leads to wasteful, overlong dramatization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and hierarchy of narrative modes
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelist must understand and deploy the relative uses and values of scene, picture, panorama, generalized narrative, and consciousness-centered report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide which mode suits each portion of the story (scene for climaxes, picture for survey, panoramic for breadth, consciousness for intimacy). The craft requires a working theory of how these modes interrelate and where each is properly used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and coherence (single form)
rubrics_metrics.description: When successfully recreated, a novel should stand as a single, compact, coherent object; unity indicates success in treatment of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After reading critically and reconstructing the work, ask whether the parts weld into a coherent whole. If the form is imperfect, trace whether the fault lies in choice of subject, divergence in treatment, or poor arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: lifelike rendering of people
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelist's command of life is measured by the vividness, conviction, and truthfulness with which characters are rendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether characters remain as 'positive facts' in memory — whether they are solid, consistent, and revealing of human nature. The presence of many interesting and remarkable people who persist in the reader's mind is a mark of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative re-creation (author's transformative work)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist liberates, completes, and re-makes material from life into imaginatively ordered scenes and conditions impossible in mere life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the author detects significance in raw life, removes the accidental, and remakes fragments into conditions where things develop according to the work's own laws — distributing imagination across a single embracing design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and buildup for dramatic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic scenes usually require preparation; without prior shaping they cannot act swiftly or sharply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the narrative builds toward scenes (through oblique narrative, picture, or incident) so that when the scene arrives it 'climches' and has maximum force rather than being an unsupported, expensive moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of time and space
rubrics_metrics.description: Different narrative devices represent time and space differently: scenes display bounded time/space, pictures traverse long periods, panoramic methods marshal wide expanses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the mode that suits the temporal and spatial demands of the material. Be mindful that a scene cannot compress more time than it dramatizes, while summary and picture can give a sense of larger dimensions economically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding squandered dramatization and gratuitous dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Many novelists 'break into dialogue' or dramatize where no decisive gain is made, thereby wasting the scene's power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique whether dramatization is justified by purpose; prefer to reserve dialogue/scenes for instances where they accomplish things other modes cannot, and avoid unnecessary dramatization that dilutes effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: The reader/critic as co-creator
rubrics_metrics.description: The critic or critical reader must function as a maker of the book in the mind — reconstructing and re-creating the form the novelist made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To judge how a book is made, the reader must actively construct it: balance reception with creative work, attend to narrative devices, and accept responsibility for completing the novel's form in memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical familiarity with narrative 'substances'
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel is made of many narrative 'substances' (forms of presentation) that the practised eye should recognize and treat distinctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a technical vocabulary and sensitivity to distinguish modes (dramatic, pictorial, scenic, generalized, consciousness-centered) so that you can perceive and appraise their capacities and demands in any given passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of consciousness-centered narration ('the mirror')
rubrics_metrics.description: When a story is centered in somebody's consciousness, the pictorial report's thinness can be overcome by making the mind that reflects (the 'mirror') a dramatized, visible object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate narratives that filter events through a constituted mind: this interposition can convert a merely pictorial report into strong dramatic material by dramatizing the reporting consciousness itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline and making the most of the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist must choose a disciplined method to make the most of a story; the 'easy way' that avoids method generally fails to realize a subject's full potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the author has disciplined choice and method to extract the richest effects from the subject; prefer approaches that maximize what can be made of the particular story rather than taking easier, narrower routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and development of critical vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical discussion suffers from an unsettled vocabulary; terms like 'dramatic', 'pictorial', 'scenic', 'generalized' need clearer definitions to be useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and writers should aim to sharpen and standardize terms that distinguish narrative modes and their functions; precise terminology aids in instruction, judgement, and craft development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and respect limits of criticism (humility about exactness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the book-vague, shifting, and memory-imperfect — criticism cannot be exact; statements are approximate and the critic must be modest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the limitations of recall and language, but nonetheless pursue the practical task of reconstructing and studying the book's making; accept inexactness while aiming for the closest, workmanlike account possible.
